bihar_raw_news.content: Home · e-Governance News Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary. Photo: Information and Public Relations Department, Government of Bihar / Wikimedia Commons Bihar is preparing to move its Cabinet from paper files to a fully digital workflow. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on 4 November 2026 directed officials to roll out the state’s e-Cabinet system soon, so that every Cabinet-related file and decision is handled on a digital platform, The Times of India reported . The review was held at the Sankalp Sabhagar in Lok Sevak Awas, Patna. It follows other recent digital steps in the state, including the UPYOG portal linking all 264 urban local bodies . What the Bihar e-Cabinet system will change Under the plan, the movement and processing of Cabinet files will be 100 per cent digital. According to the state’s release, carried by UNI and ANI, the system is meant to: Make Cabinet decision-making faster, simpler and more transparent Cut the time taken to process and move files between departments Improve coordination among departments and speed up execution of decisions Fix administrative accountability at each stage of a file Reduce the use of paper, saving time, money and resources AI to simplify administrative processes The Chief Minister asked officials to make full use of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, within the e-Cabinet system so that complex administrative procedures become simpler. He called the system a milestone for good governance and digital administration in Bihar, and said the government was committed to a more efficient, transparent and people-centric administration. Choudhary, who was sworn in as Bihar Chief Minister in April 2026 , chaired the review himself, a sign that the rollout is being treated as a near-term deliverable. Who presented the roadmap Arvind Kumar Choudhary, Additional Chief Secretary of the Cabinet Secretariat Department, gave a presentation on the digital model, operating framework, technical aspects and implementation roadmap of the e-Cabinet. Secretaries to the Chief Minister Lokesh Kumar Singh and Sanjay Kumar Singh, and Special Secretary of the Cabinet Secretariat Department Arvind Kumar Verma, also attended. The department’s leadership was part of a recent reshuffle of senior IAS officers in Bihar . No launch date has been announced yet. The meeting was a preparedness review, and the government has not said whether the system will start with a pilot or a full rollout. Why it matters Paperless Cabinet working extends the e-Office approach that many governments have adopted, such as Maharashtra’s e-Office journey , to the highest level of state decision-making. For a state of Bihar’s size, faster file movement at Cabinet level could shorten the time between a decision and its delivery to citizens. Key takeaways Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary has ordered an early rollout of the e-Cabinet system. All Cabinet files and decision processes will move to a digital platform. AI tools are to be used to simplify administrative procedures. ACS Arvind Kumar Choudhary presented the implementation roadmap; no go-live date yet. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar plans free sugarcane seed distribution to revive Raiyam, Sakri sugar mills
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News Darbhanga: The Bihar government has begun efforts to expand sugarcane cultivation in areas surrounding the long-closed Raiyam and Sakri sugar mills, with plans to provide farmers with improved varieties of sugarcane seeds free of cost, Jagran reported. The initiative is aimed at increasing sugarcane production in the region ahead of the proposed revival of the two mills, which have remained closed for more than three decades. Farmers will be able to start cultivation without having to purchase seeds. The deadline for submitting applications under the scheme has been extended to November 16. The sugarcane area expansion programme has been launched to ensure an adequate supply of raw material for the Raiyam mill and the Sakri mill in Madhubani district. The government aims to encourage large-scale sugarcane cultivation in areas around the mills so that sufficient cane is available when operations resume. Under the scheme, farmers will receive seeds of improved sugarcane varieties free of charge. The department is also organising farmers’ meetings, workshops and training programmes to familiarise growers with modern cultivation practices. Financial assistance is being provided to reduce the initial cost of cultivation and encourage more farmers to take up sugarcane farming. Ajit Kumar, Assistant Director of the Sugarcane Department, said farmers can apply online for the scheme until November 16. The earlier deadline was October 31. Applications must be submitted through the department’s official website, ccs.bihar.gov.in. Farmers holding between 0.25 acre and 2.5 acres of land are eligible for the scheme. Applicants must provide their land revenue receipt and sugarcane registration ID while submitting the online application. Expanding sugarcane cultivation is being seen as an important step towards restarting the Raiyam and Sakri mills. Increased cane production could offer farmers an alternative crop and, if the mills resume operations, create employment and business opportunities in the region. Thousands of people in the Mithilanchal region are expected to benefit directly and indirectly from the revival of the mills.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Diaspora Investment Gets Two New Portals for 2027 Meet - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar Diaspora Investment Gets Two New Portals for 2027 Meet Breaking News Bihar Diaspora Investment Gets Two New Portals for 2027 Meet By Ayesha Siddiqui November 5, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has launched two digital portals to connect the state’s diaspora with its development activities and attract investment ahead of the Bihar Business Connect-2027 global investors’ meet. The portals were unveiled during the Bihar Foundation’s ‘Samvad’ programme, which brought together representatives of all 55 national and international chapters through video conferencing. The Bihar Foundation Portal is intended to provide a structured digital link between people of Bihari origin and the state. According to the report, it will include online registration, an integrated database and information about chapter activities. Representatives will also be able to upload details and photographs of programmes conducted through the network. The second platform, the Bihar Business Connect-2027 Portal, will focus on participation in the upcoming investors’ meet. It will allow users to register, receive event updates and access information about investment and industrial opportunities in Bihar. The two portals place the Bihar Foundation’s existing network at the centre of the state government’s outreach and investment strategy. The organisation currently has 55 active chapters, comprising 31 international and 24 national chapters. The government plans to expand the network to 100 chapters by the end of the next financial year. The state also plans to establish 10 integrated centres across the country. These centres are intended to promote investment, business and tourism activities, adding a physical institutional layer to the digital engagement being developed through the new portals. The launch programme included Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Kumar Choudhary, industries minister Shreyasi Singh and other officials. Industries department secretary-cum-Bihar Foundation chief executive officer Kundan Kumar conducted the proceedings. Addressing the programme, Choudhary said the government wanted to connect people of Bihari origin with their roots and encourage them to contribute their experience, knowledge and resources to the state’s development. He said the diaspora could help strengthen Bihar’s economy and attract investment. The initiative combines three functions that are often handled separately by state governments: maintaining a diaspora database, coordinating overseas and domestic chapters, and presenting investment opportunities to prospective participants. The government’s stated plan is to use the Bihar Foundation’s wider network to support business, investment and tourism outreach. The portals also create a central channel for information ahead of Business Connect-2027, although the report does not specify the investment sectors, project pipeline, financial commitments or implementation timeline for individual opportunities. The next stated expansion milestones are the creation of additional Bihar Foundation chapters and the establishment of 10 integrated centres across the country. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar rolls out red carpet for renewable energy investors - MillenniumPost
bihar_raw_news.content: Home > Business > Bihar rolls out red carpet for renewable energy investors Business Bihar rolls out red carpet for renewable energy investors BY Mpost Bureau 5 Nov 2026 1:02 AM IST X Mpost Bureau 5 Nov 2026 1:02 AM IST New Delhi: Bihar on Wednesday pitched investment opportunities worth Rs 2.57 lakh crore in its power sector, inviting domestic and international investors to explore projects in renewable energy, storage, transmission and distribution. Addressing the Bihar State Plenary Session at the India Renewable Energy Summit and Expo 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, state Energy Minister Shailesh Kumar alias Bulo Mandal assured investors of all possible support from the government and said Bihar offered significant potential for high growth and returns. He said the state’s electricity demand had increased from around 700 MW in 2005 to nearly 10,000 MW, with every household now having electricity connectivity. Energy Secretary and Bihar State Power Holding Company Ltd (BSPHCL) CMD Ajay Yadav said demand was projected to reach 25,000 MW over the next decade. He highlighted the 301 MW Kajra Solar Power Project, supported by a 523 MWh battery energy storage system, and said projects worth Rs 78,400 crore were at various stages of implementation. Under the Bihar Renewable Energy Policy 2025, the state has set a target of developing 24 GW renewable energy capacity and 6 GWh energy storage capacity by 2030. A comprehensive investment roadmap of Rs 2,57,316 crore has also been prepared. Three MoUs were signed during the summit involving BSPGCL, MANIT Bhopal, the Power Sector Skill Council, BSPHCL, Bihar Power Training Management Society and TERI to promote renewable energy. bihar_raw_news.title: Patna-Purnia Expressway May Get Launch Nod During PM's Vaishali Visit - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Patna-Purnia Expressway May Get Launch Nod During PM’s Vaishali Visit Breaking News Patna-Purnia Expressway May Get Launch Nod During PM’s Vaishali Visit By Ayesha Siddiqui November 5, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to visit Vaishali on November 20 for a public programme where he may launch or lay the foundation for several Bihar development projects, including the proposed Patna-Purnia Expressway, according to state BJP leaders quoted by the Times of India. The proposed National Expressway-9, described as Bihar’s first national expressway project, is planned as a six-lane greenfield corridor. It will begin at Mirnagar in Vaishali district and pass through Samastipur, Darbhanga, Saharsa and Madhepura before ending at Chand Bhatti in Purnia district. The details of the proposed visit and project programme were shared by BJP functionaries ahead of the planned event. The report said the Prime Minister was scheduled to participate in a public programme at the Jafarpatti Industrial Area in Vaishali, although the project launches were described as expected or likely rather than formally confirmed through a government notification. Bihar BJP president Sanjay Saraogi inspected the proposed venue and reviewed arrangements with officials. He also discussed logistical preparations and directed those involved in organising the programme to ensure its smooth conduct. BJP MLAs Awadhesh Singh and Sanjay Singh, along with Janata Dal (United) MLA Siddharth Patel, were present during the inspection. The Patna-Purnia corridor would connect central and northern parts of Bihar through a route crossing several districts. The proposed alignment includes Samastipur, Darbhanga, Saharsa and Madhepura, placing the expressway within a wider regional transport network linking Vaishali with Purnia in eastern Bihar. The Prime Minister is also expected to inaugurate or lay foundation stones for projects in Bhagalpur and Banka districts during the programme. These may include a proposed Central University near Vikramshila and the proposed Ajgaibinath Greenfield Airport near Sultanganj in Bhagalpur district. Saraogi said the visit would provide fresh momentum to development initiatives in Bihar and help accelerate investment and infrastructure growth in the state. The source report did not provide the expressway’s construction cost, completion schedule, land-acquisition status, detailed interchange plan or traffic projections. Further details about the final project list, the formal launch arrangements and the implementation timelines are expected to be clarified ahead of the proposed November 20 programme. national_raw_news.title: RSS annual meeting to conclude today in Indore 04 Nov 2026 | 2:16 PM 122
national_raw_news.content: The three-day Akhil Bharatiya Karyakari Mandal Meeting of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh concluded in Indore today. RSS chief Dr Mohan Bhagwat, General Secretary Dattatreya Hosabale and around 400 office-bearers and representatives from across the country attended the meeting. The discussions included a review of the Centenary Year programmes, expansion of the organisation, opening of new shakhas and the growing problem of drug addiction among youth. Plans related to education, expansion of RSS activities abroad and taking the Panch Parivartan (five social changes) to the people were also discussed. After the meeting, RSS General Secretary Dattatreya Hosabale addressed the media and spoke on several important issues. On reservation, he said that the system should continue for backward communities as long as social backwardness exists. On the issue of RSS registration, he said that the RSS is a part of society and works according to the laws of the country. Mr Hosabale stressed the need to connect young people with positive activities and keep them away from drug addiction. He said that the younger generation is also falling prey to addiction and RSS volunteers are working to address this issue. He also informed that RSS volunteers had carried out relief work in areas affected by floods and cyclones. In Assam’s Sivasagar and Jorhat districts, more than 1,600 volunteers provided food, water and medicines to around 42,200 families. They also provided support to around 150 families for rebuilding their houses. Help was also provided to farmers, fishermen and other affected families in cyclone-hit areas of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi hails Cabinet decisions on faster justice, energy storage and critical minerals
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday welcomed Union Cabinet decisions on fast-track courts, energy storage, statistical reforms and critical mineral processing, saying they would accelerate justice delivery, strengthen energy security and build domestic capabilities. In posts on X, the Prime Minister highlighted the continuation of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Fast Track Special Courts, including exclusive POCSO courts, for five years from April 1, 2026. “From less delay to faster justice,” he said. The scheme has a total outlay of Rs 3,788.04 crore, comprising a Central share of Rs 2,353.15 crore and a state and Union Territory share of Rs 1,434.89 crore. The Central contribution will come from the Nirbhaya Fund. PM Modi also welcomed the Rs 14,500 crore Viability Gap Funding Scheme to develop 92 GWh of grid-scale energy storage capacity, saying it would support investment of nearly Rs 1 lakh crore. The five-year scheme, running until 2030–31, will support 60 GWh of pumped hydro storage, 30 GWh of battery energy storage and 2 GWh through emerging storage technologies. Battery storage projects will require a minimum domestic content of 40 per cent. “Store More → Import Less → Power India Round the Clock!” the Prime Minister said, adding that the initiative would improve power reliability, enable greater renewable energy integration and strengthen energy security. On the Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research (VISTAR), PM Modi said the scheme would modernise India’s statistical system through technology, artificial intelligence, a focus on detailed local-level data and integrated statistical systems. “Better data means better decisions, better policies and better delivery to people,” he said. The Prime Minister also highlighted the Cabinet’s approval of a scheme to strengthen domestic processing of critical minerals, including lithium, nickel and cobalt, which are essential for electric vehicles, batteries, electronics and defence. He said India remained heavily dependent on imported refined materials and needed to develop its own processing capabilities. The scheme’s key features include new critical mineral processing plants, capital subsidies to encourage investment, greater domestic value addition and stronger supply chains. “The principle is clear…India must have capabilities to build technologies of the future!” PM Modi said.

national_raw_news.title: Government of Odisha partners signs MOU with J-PAL South Asia to strengthen evidence ...
national_raw_news.content: Government of Odisha partners signs MOU with J-PAL South Asia to strengthen evidence-based policymaking Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Government of Odisha partners signs MOU with J-PAL South Asia to strengthen evidence-based policymaking ANI | Updated: Nov 05, 2026 08:16 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Bhubaneswar( Odisha ) [India], November 5 (ANI): The Government of Odisha and the Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (J-PAL) South Asia on Wednesday signed a three-year Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen evidence-based policymaking across the state. J-PAL South Asia, hosted at the Institute for Financial Management and Research (IFMR) in Chennai, will work with departments to identify priority policy challenges, generate rigorous evidence, and translate research findings into actionable policy recommendations. According to the press release by Governemnt of Odisha , the MoU was signed by Rashmi Kabi, FA-cum-Additional Secretary, Planning & Convergence Department, Government of Odisha , and Shobhini Mukerji, Executive Director, J-PAL South Asia, in the presence of Anu Garg, Chief Secretary, Government of Odisha , Deoranjan Kumar Singh, Development Commissioner-cum-Additional Chief Secretary to Govt; Murali Mallikarjunan, Acting Associate Director, Policy, J-PAL South Asia; and Secretaries from across the state Govt. departments. Odisha Vision 2036 and 2047 charts the state’s path to becoming Samruddha Odisha by 2036 and Viksit Odisha by 2047. The partnership builds on J-PAL South Asia’s engagement in Odisha since 2006, spanning early childhood education, foundational literacy and numeracy, governance, sanitation, agriculture and gender. Under the MoU, the Government has invited J-PAL South Asia to support its vision, with J-PAL coordinating with departments to understand their policy priorities. It includes Barnali, the gender-equity curriculum now being taught in about 23,000 government schools, where J-PAL South Asia serves as the knowledge and research partner to the School & Mass Education Department and Breakthrough Trust, the release said. The partnership will be guided by a Steering Committee chaired by the Chief Secretary, comprising senior government officials and representatives from J-PAL South Asia. The Committee will meet every six months to review project proposals, while nodal officers from both sides will coordinate activities. The scope and deliverables of individual projects will be developed in consultation with the relevant departments. Anu Garg, Chief Secretary, Government of Odisha , said, “We have set ourselves an ambitious goal of Viksit Odisha for Viksit Bharat. Our Vision commits us to engaging research institutions in policy research and piloting innovations, as well as adopting data- and AI-based interventions in line with global best practices. I see J-PAL South Asia's role as threefold. First, to bring the most relevant global evidence to bear on our priorities; second, to work with our departments to adapt promising approaches to Odisha ’s needs; and third, to support us in designing and testing evidence- and data-based solutions before they are taken to scale.” Shobhini Mukerji, Executive Director, J-PAL South Asia said, " Odisha has long been a pioneer in generating and using evidence.
